title: Entanglement Capacity Estimates and Throughput Measurements of Quantum Channels
problem: Theoretical entangled qubit capacity estimates and practical throughput measurements (ebps) of quantum networks are difficult to relate due to lack of precise measurements with matching analytical models. Previous capacity estimates using light measurements do not consistently align with actual throughput measurements.
motivation: Characterizing throughput performance of quantum networks is essential for understanding and optimizing entangled qubit distribution systems that enable quantum communications and computing infrastructure.
method: Physical measurements on a fiber-based testbed (0-75 km) use single photon coincidence detectors to derive transmissivity approximations and estimate normalized analytic capacity. Capacity estimates are converted to throughput bounds (ebps) using a multiplier from co-located detector measurements. Results are validated against actual measured throughput across all test connections.
key_novelty: Establishing a concrete, experimentally-validated relationship between theoretical capacity estimates and measured throughput by using matched physical measurements and analytical models on a real quantum channel testbed.
contributions: Physical testbed measurements of entangled qubit throughput on fiber connections up to 75 km with photonic entanglement sources and single photon detectors
Methodology for converting analytical capacity estimates to throughput bounds using detector-based multipliers
Validation that measured throughput is consistently upper-bounded by analytical capacity across all tested connections
Identification that previous light-based capacity estimates fail to account for C-band transmission limitations with distance, causing non-representative estimates

metrics.other: throughput measured in ebps (entangled bit pairs per second)
metrics.accuracy: consistency between measured throughput and analytical capacity bounds across 0-75 km fiber connections

baselines: theoretical capacity models without distance-based C-band considerations
limitations: Evaluation limited to fiber-based quantum channels up to 75 km; other quantum channel types and longer-distance scenarios not explored.
primary_theme: Quantum network performance characterization and measurement
